title: Check yourself: lambda syntax and overloads

questions.stem: A metrics library has `void record(String name, ToLongFunction<Event> f)`. A release adds `void record(String name, Function<Event, Duration> f)`. A caller has `metrics.record("bytes", (var e) -> e.size())`, where `size()` returns `long`. What happens when the caller rebuilds?

options.text: It compiles and calls the ToLongFunction overload, since `var` gives the parameter a declared type the compiler can check the body against
options.says: to the compiler a var parameter is still inferred, so the body isn't type-checked while the overload is chosen

options.text: It compiles and calls the ToLongFunction overload, since the compiler sees that `e.size()` returns a long and not a Duration
options.says: for an inferred lambda the compiler looks only at the body's shape while choosing an overload, and an expression body fits both

options.text: It fails to compile, since the parameter's type is inferred and an expression body fits both overloads
options.says: an implicitly typed lambda (var included) can't choose between same-arity overloads when its expression body fits both

options.text: It fails to compile, since `var` on a lambda parameter is allowed only together with an annotation or `final`
options.says: a bare var parameter such as (var s) -> s.strip() compiles; annotations and final are what var makes possible, not what it requires

origin.section: An Implicitly Typed Lambda Can't Choose Between Overloads of the Same Arity

questions.stem: A cache holds "v1" under key k-17. A service runs `Future<?> f = pool.submit(() -> cache.remove("k-17"));` on an ExecutorService, where `remove` returns the value it removed. What does `f.get()` return once the task has run?

options.text: It returns null, since the lambda has no `return` statement and is therefore passed as a Runnable
options.says: an expression body that is a method call fits both Runnable and Callable; having no return statement doesn't make it a Runnable

options.text: It returns "v1", since the body fits both interfaces and the Callable overload is preferred when it does
options.says: a statement expression fits both interfaces; when the parameter types are known (here there are none), the value-returning overload wins

options.text: It returns null, since the body fits both interfaces and the Runnable overload is preferred when it does
options.says: the preference goes the other way: the overload whose method returns a value wins

options.text: It returns "v1", since `submit` keeps the task's value even when the task is passed as a Runnable
options.says: the braced body, which goes to the Runnable overload, gives get() = null; the value is there only because Callable was chosen

origin.section: When a Body Fits Both, the Overload That Returns a Value Wins

questions.stem: A developer writes `Function<Order, String> label = o -> { if (o.rush()) return "RUSH"; else if (o.total() > 100) return "BIG"; };` What does javac do with it?

options.text: It accepts it, and `label` returns null for an order that is neither rush nor over 100, since a lambda's missing value defaults to null
options.says: a block that can reach its closing brace is not value-compatible, so javac rejects it as missing a return value

options.text: It accepts it, and `label` throws for an order that is neither rush nor over 100, since the missing path is checked when the lambda runs
options.says: the check is made at compile time: a block whose end is reachable can't be a value-returning body

options.text: It rejects it, since control can reach the end of the block without a value, so the body can't return a String
options.says: value-compatible needs every return to carry a value and the end of the block to be unreachable; javac reports a missing return value

options.text: It rejects it, since an if-else chain is allowed in a lambda body only when it is written as a conditional expression
options.says: block bodies on the page use if statements freely; the error is the path that reaches the end without a return

origin.section: A Body's Shape Decides Whether It Returns a Value, Nothing, or Either

questions.stem: A team declares `interface Convert { <T> T convert(String raw, Class<T> type); }` and writes `Convert c = (raw, type) -> type.cast(raw);`. What follows?

options.text: It compiles, since the lambda's parameter types are inferred afresh for each call's T
options.says: a lambda has nowhere to declare a type parameter, so it can't implement a generic method

options.text: It compiles once the parameters are declared as `(String raw, Class<T> type)`, since that names the type the method needs
options.says: there is no T in scope for the lambda to name (javac reports cannot find symbol T), and the method it would implement is still generic, so a lambda can't fit

options.text: It is rejected, since a lambda can't declare a type parameter; a method reference to a generic method can implement it
options.says: javac reports that the method is generic; a method reference, an anonymous class, or a generic interface instead of a generic method fixes it

options.text: It is rejected, since an interface whose one abstract method is generic isn't functional; only a class can implement it
options.says: a method reference to a generic method fits such an interface, so a class is not the only way

origin.section: A Lambda Can't Implement a Generic Method
